questions.stem: In sickle cell anaemia, what causes the change in haemoglobin shape?

options.text: The haemoglobin has too many polypeptide chains
A single amino acid substitution (glutamic acid to valine) alters the protein's folding
A change in temperature denatures the protein
Iron is missing from the haemoglobin molecule

questions.explanation: In sickle cell anaemia, just one amino acid change (glutamic acid replaced by valine) in the haemoglobin molecule changes its shape and causes the red blood cells to become sickle-shaped. This shows how important amino acid sequence is.
